ops.title: Oversized transcript event: record bound lives in cc-transcript-owner; deadline skips share the cause
ops.body:
Defect 485@9fe58747 (lane dd-339598808-fix, codex on Sprite pool-fqr6jmloxafubp5r, capt-hookd 12.121.40). Evidence: that Sprite's ~/.cache/captain-hook/logs/01a1b259-ca3c-7920-a914-12833e01d38f.log, 207 "transcript event over the record bound skipped" lines from 19:35:58 UTC.

Where the bound lives. The 1 MiB record bound is enforced inside the Rust snapshot host, cc-transcript-owner (yasyf/cc-transcript rust/crates/core/src/snapshot_codec.rs MAX_RECORD_BYTES, Bound::write; events projection at snapshot_projection.rs:2171-2201, turns at 2056 and 3837, tool_calls at 2392 and 3170). captain-hook's Python client never receives the oversized record: it gets only an output_limit refusal, bisects the event range in RemoteSession._windowed (captain_hook/snapshots/client.py:1642), and skip_oversized drops the single event. So the record cannot be clipped in client.py; the clip has to happen where the record is encoded, in cc-transcript. No integrity hash covers record content (snapshot_owned.rs hashes the request context only), and the decoder takes a clipped string field as is, so clipping in the host breaks no protocol.

What actually loses the call. has_command, has_tool, has_read, has_override, has_command_regex (RanCommand, UsedTool, ReadFile) and predicate_inputs are evaluated inside the host and return a bool or a record without tool output, so they still see the call today. What loses it: hooks that iterate .events or .turns (the one event is dropped with an evidence gap), and tool_calls readers (ToolUseWire carries the result, so the whole query fails output_limit and the guard fails open). A turn record carries the output twice (the event and the tool use's result).

Transport-deadline skips (item 2). They follow from the oversized event. Each PostToolUse dispatch re-bisects to it: about 15-20 failed host queries of 10-40 ms each, every one re-encoding the 2 MB event (LimitedWriter to the bound, then a full Counter pass for the refusal text). Two hooks in the same dispatch (request prefixes 4609d55c and 93067ea0, log lines 115-165) then hit the 0.75 s foreground deadline: owner_thread_words_write_rows and owner_messages_get_eyes skipped with "snapshot transport deadline elapsed". Nothing remembers the oversized index, so every later dispatch pays the bisection again. Keeping the event on the first query removes both.
